[2026-08-12T10:55:29Z] Why the code-review severity axes are inert — zero-LLM root cause (analysis record)
(migrated from childsafe-bizarre-lorikeet comment 10 — session-scoped ops/analysis record; original comment retained there, see the index comment on that ticket)

# Why the code-review severity axes are inert — root cause, zero-LLM (2026-08-12)

Operator question before approving Phase 3: *"consider why they're inert before acting on this.
we see very few code review findings."* Answer: **the axes are inert because the block decision
does not read them for 98.5% of findings — not because they are uninformative, and not because
the reviewer finds little.** The ≤0.77% level-collapse flip rate recorded above is a *confounded*
measurement. Corpus: all 1,545 `code_review` sidecar events in the tracker (3,839 findings),
re-scored offline through the shipped `rebar.llm.review_kernel.decide.impact`.

## 1. Distribution headline

| metric | value |
|---|---|
| code-review runs | 1,545 |
| findings | 3,839 — advisory 2,852 / dropped 913 / indeterminate 34 / **blocking 40** |
| verdicts | PASS 1,500 (97.1%) · BLOCK 39 (2.5%) · INDETERMINATE 6 |
| reviews with **0 blocking** | 1,506 / 1,545 = **97.5%** |
| reviews with **0 findings at all** | 470 / 1,545 = 30.4% |
| findings per review | median **2**, mean 2.48 (mode: 0, then 2, then 1) |
| tier | LLM 3,772 · DET 59 |
| **blocking by tier** | **DET 30 · LLM 2 · untiered 8** |

The operator's "0–2 advisory non-blocking" observation is exactly right and is the *normal* mode.
But the reviewer is **not** quiet: it emits 2.48 findings/run and self-labels **183 of them
`major` or `critical`** (159 major + 24 critical). **Every one of those 183 landed in `advisory`
except 2.** The LLM's total contribution to the block decision across the whole corpus is
**2 findings in 1,545 reviews (0.13%)**. Blocking is effectively a *deterministic* gate:
`bugfix-size-attestation` (27) + `sec`/`security` (10) + `secret-detection` (3).

Top advisory criteria: tests 1,399 · maintainability 672 · correctness 617 · edge-cases 415 ·
regression 284 · error-handling 172. Top dropped: docs 328 · tests 169 · maintainability 145.

## 2. Root cause — two structural AND-gates, neither of which is severity

**(i) Blocking is criterion-routed, not severity-routed.** Cross-tab of
`block_threshold` × `blocking_enabled` × `tier`:

```
(0.95, False, LLM)  3353     <- 98.2% of scored findings: blocking DISABLED
(0.54, True,  LLM)    51     <- the ONLY blocking-enabled criterion: `security`
(0.90, False, LLM)    10     <- project.review-phase-boundaries, also disabled
(None, None,  DET)    59     <- deterministic, no axes at all
```

Only `security` (51 findings, 1.3%) is blocking-enabled. For the other 3,363, the severity axes
are graded, serialized, and then discarded — the decision was fixed by routing before `impact()`
was consulted.

**(ii) For those 3,363, the 0.95 threshold is functionally unreachable.** `impact()` is
`(max(prod,debt) + blast + likelihood + reversibility) / 4`, each term ∈ {0.33, 0.67, 1.0}.
Exhaustive enumeration of all 432 attribute combinations:

- **7 / 432 combos (1.6%) reach ≥ 0.95**, and **all 7 require the exact conjunction
  `blast_radius=system` AND `likelihood=high` AND `reversibility=hard`** (plus prod or debt =
  high). The threshold is not a severity dial — it is a hard 3-way AND on the rarest level of
  three axes.
- The next attainable score below 0.95 is **0.9175**. There is a **dead zone**: no finding can
  ever score in (0.9175, 0.95).

Observed marginals over 3,738 graded findings: `blast_radius=system` **92** · `likelihood=high`
**246** · `reversibility=hard` **7** · **all-three conjunction: 0 (zero) occurrences.**

Empirical impact distribution: p50 **0.30**, p90 0.32, p99 0.60, **max 0.90**. Median gap to
threshold **0.65**; only 12 of 3,414 findings land within 0.10 of their threshold. The axes are
never exercised anywhere near the decision boundary because **the boundary is outside the
observed — and nearly outside the attainable — range.**

**(iii) Even the one live path is degenerate.** All 7 findings that ever met their threshold
scored *exactly* 0.54 (= the threshold), and only **2** became blocking: blocking on `security`
additionally requires `validity == 1.0`. Findings at impact 0.54 with validity 0.857 or 0.714
stayed advisory. On that path `impact` behaves as a **binary** (0.54 fires vs ~0.30 doesn't),
and the real discriminator is validity, not the ordinal ladder.

## 3. Hypotheses adjudicated

- **(a) "few findings, mostly advisory — axes never exercised near the threshold"** —
  **TRUE but it is the symptom, not the cause.** Median gap-to-threshold 0.65 confirms the
  non-exercise; §2 explains why it is structural, not a volume artifact. Adding 10x the findings
  would not move it.
- **(b) "threshold/aggregation crushes variance — mean-of-attributes dilution"
  (idea `neat-sooty-termite`)** — **CONFIRMED, and the ticket understates it.** It is not merely
  that the mean dilutes a high-severity axis; it is that mean-of-4 against a 0.95 cut collapses
  the whole 5-axis ordinal space into a 3-way AND satisfied 0 times in 3,738 gradings, with a
  0.9175→0.95 dead zone. **This is the root cause.**
- **(c) "reviewer genuinely finds little (fleet effect: clean changes)"** — **REFUTED as the
  primary cause.** 3,839 findings, 2.48/run, only 30% zero-finding runs, 183 self-labeled
  major/critical. The reviewer finds plenty; what is rare is *blocking*, not *finding*. (A
  fleet effect may well contribute to severity being mostly `minor` — 2,161 of 3,839 — but it
  cannot explain 183 major/critical findings passing.)
- **(d) "reviewer under-reports (prompt/calibration reluctance)"** — **REFUTED for severity
  labelling.** The model applies `critical`/`major` freely and its labels are simply not
  consulted by the gate. The weekly series shows **no reporting decay**: advisory/run runs
  2.91 (W28), 2.07, 1.10, 1.73, 2.01, 2.20 (W33) — stationary, no step-down after any
  calibration/prompt/routing commit. The rise in blocking (W32: 21, W33: 10, vs 0–8 before) is
  fully attributable to the **DET** criteria `secret-detection` and `bugfix-size-attestation`
  first appearing in W32 (commit `1920dc9fe5` "Escalate big bug fixes to real review") — i.e.
  the gate got teeth from *deterministic* checks, not from LLM severity.
  A separate *recall* question remains open (round-2 measured Nova Pro at ~50–57% blocking-
  criteria recall on plan-review), but under-reporting is **not** why the axes are inert.

**Verdict: (b) is the cause; (a) is its symptom; (c) and (d) are refuted as primary.**

## 4. Recommendation on Phase 3 — do NOT proceed as scoped

The migration plan's post-audit note concludes "Phase 3 is UNBLOCKED and LOW-RISK: code-review's
ordinal ladder carries almost no decision weight … so its migration or simplification can
proceed." **That inference does not hold on this evidence.** The ≤0.77% flip rate measures a
ladder wired to a decision that is switched off — it is evidence of *disconnection*, not of
*uninformativeness*. You cannot conclude an instrument is uncalibrated by reading it while it
is unplugged. Migrating ordinals→kind-sets under that measurement would:

1. **Bake in the defect.** A kind-set reconstruction validated against "flips ≤0.77%" is
   validated against a constant function. Any kind set — including a random one — passes.
2. **Spend the change budget on the wrong layer.** The ordinal encoding is not what makes
   code-review pass everything; routing (`blocking_enabled=False` on 98.2%) and an unreachable
   0.95 cut are.
3. **Make the real defect harder to see later**, by rewriting the very fields that currently
   document it.

**Sequence instead:**

- **P3.0 (zero-LLM, do first) — fix the threshold/aggregation, then re-measure.** Either lower
  the non-security cut into the attainable range (the corpus p99 is 0.60; the 0.9175 ceiling
  means anything above ~0.92 is a no-op), or replace mean-of-4 with a max/floor rule so one
  `high`+`system` axis is not averaged away by three `easy`/`local` ones. Decide separately
  and deliberately **which criteria should be blocking-enabled** — today it is exactly one.
  This is a policy question for the operator, not a modelling one.
- **P3.1 — re-run `code_decisiveness.py` against the corrected decision rule.** Only then does
  the flip rate mean anything. If the axes still flip <1% *with a live threshold*, the
  ordinal→kind-set migration is justified and cheap. If they flip materially, Phase 2's
  "reconstruct levels deterministically" discipline applies here too.
- **Phase 3 as currently written: hold.** Not "pointless" — **premature and, on the current
  justification, actively wrong.**

Cheap intermediate sanity check, zero-LLM: replay the 183 existing `major`/`critical` LLM
findings through a candidate decision rule and inspect how many *should* have blocked. No new
inference calls; the findings and their axes are already recorded.

## 5. If you still want an under-reporting probe (not needed for Phase 3)

Under-reporting is refuted for *labelling*, but *recall* is untested for code-review. Cheapest
confirmation: replay N historically-defective changes through `review-code` and count catches.
Sourcing gold: commits that were later reverted, or whose ticket has a `discovered_from` child
filed as a bug against them. At the measured **$1.42/run** code-review cost, **N=20 ≈ $28**,
**N=30 ≈ $43** (single epoch; double for 2-epoch stability). Recommend **N=20, one epoch, ~$28**
— and only *after* P3.0, since a recall probe against a gate that cannot block measures the
finder in isolation and tells you nothing about the gate. **Not run; approval required.**

*(Analysis-only. Zero LLM calls. Scripts are ad-hoc re-scores through the shipped `impact()`;
method matches round2/code_decisiveness.py with the field-shape correction applied.)*

[2026-08-12T20:11:47Z] Deprecation removal-readiness survey — summary (analysis record)
(migrated from childsafe-bizarre-lorikeet comment 11 — session-scoped analysis record; the full survey text is retained on that ticket's comment 11, and per-item cross-reference comments were posted on the tickets that acted on it)

Scope: "what was deprecated in prior releases that we can now remove?" Surveyed rebar._deprecations (the central registry), docs/ + CHANGELOG.md + release-notes.md + api-stability.md + migrations.md, ADR 0050, the tracker, and live origin/tickets store data (81,840 commits; 1,884 active SNAPSHOT blobs).

HEADLINE. Nothing with a recorded removal condition had met it. rebar is at 0.11.0; every scheduled deprecation carries remove_in="v1.0.0" (_deprecations.py:47), and docs/api-stability.md:30 adds an independent floor (an alias survives at least one minor release AFTER its replacement ships). The real lever is precedent, not schedule: release-notes.md:226/:249 record two completed pre-1.0 breaking passes that removed scheduled shims early by operator ruling. So the actionable question was "do we open a third pre-1.0 breaking window, and what goes in it?" — which is what the operator then did.

TIERS.
- Tier 1, ready now: the retired .gitattributes migration arm (init.py:600-616 + _RETIRED_GITATTRIBUTES_LINES at :69), ~15 LOC, permanently unreachable in this store. -> became task checked-unhelpful-tanager (e654-58e2-0d38-48c6), now CLOSED.
- Tier 2, new pre-1.0 window (operator call): (a) single-pass review public surfaces (CLI `rebar review`, lib rebar.llm.review_ticket, MCP review_ticket) — key scoping finding: the ENGINE _review_ticket_impl must STAY (three live internal consumers: _mcp_llm.py:92-95, llm/review_workflows.py:86, llm/evals/eval_solver.py:348), so removal deletes only three thin entry points; schemas/review_result.schema.json also stays. -> priceless-charred-fruitbat (97d4-3098-2fb6-4658), now CLOSED. (b) REBAR_LLM_MODEL / llm.model, a supersession by [tool.rebar.llm.model_classes], small. -> slowmotion-stricken-mare (6cc4-56f1-6cc6-4c7f), now CLOSED.
- Tier 3, blocked on a named condition: resolved_statuses keys — CRITICAL distinction, reconciler.resolved_statuses is LIVE (Jira Data Center adapter, settings.py:101 -> backend.py:303) and is NOT a removal candidate; only jira.resolved_statuses is inert. Hard-removal follow-up salted-growable-murrelet (f408-64ad-ee41-46b6) is deliberately blocked on operator sign-off. Also fastmcp/mcp 2.0 (epic bared-nickel-insect): premise corrected — standalone fastmcp is not a dependency at all; rebar uses the bundled mcp.server.fastmcp pinned mcp>=1.28.1,<2, and ADR 0050 explicitly REJECTED the standalone stack. Not a removal; a future forward migration with six hard-blocking import sites. Also the event-schema/reducer compat folds: NOT REMOVABLE essentially permanently (1,118/1,884 active snapshots hold creation_channel "unknown"; 265 lack file_impact_scope; 155 lack plan_review_phase) — removing any would silently mis-project ~1,100 tickets. One narrow cold-but-keep exception: the attestations fold-in inner body (_processors.py:727-735, reducer/_cache.py:99-106), 588 snapshots enter, zero fold.
- Tier 4, needs operator decision (deprecated by policy, no recorded condition): 4-digit/two-quad short-ID acceptance (_ids.py:53/:256) — no registry row, no window, effectively unexercised in identity-sensitive artifacts (60/60 recent trailers use the full canonical id); and the unregistered CLI compat aliases verify-authorship and bridge-status, which must be REGISTERED and announced before they are removable at all.

POSITIVE FINDING (registry hygiene). The deprecation registry is complete and trustworthy: warn_deprecated raises KeyError on an unregistered surface, and tests/unit/test_deprecation_registry.py source-scans for raw emissions bypassing it. The only warnings.warn in src/rebar outside _deprecations.py is an unknown-frontmatter-key warning. The survey's registry-derived inventory can therefore be treated as exhaustive for signalled surfaces.

RECOMMENDATION AS GIVEN: remove item 1 only on schedule; bank items 2 and 3 in a third pre-1.0 breaking window at v0.12.0; do not touch items 4-7; announce items 8-9 before removing.

[2026-08-12T22:48:29Z] AWS alarm sweep 04:00Z→22:45Z (read-only ops investigation)
(migrated from childsafe-bizarre-lorikeet comment 12 — session-scoped ops/analysis record; original comment retained there, see the index comment on that ticket)

AWS alarm sweep 2026-08-12T04:00Z → 22:45Z (read-only; CloudWatch describe/get + SSM read-only journalctl on i-00880b2c7f13527c5; nothing mutated in AWS or on the box).

SCOPE. 14 metric alarms, 0 composite alarms; all 14 are OK right now. describe-alarm-history (StateUpdate) over the window returns 8 items, of which 3 are transitions INTO ALarm. The other 5 are recoveries and the two INSUFFICIENT_DATA→OK settles of the newly-created reason-scoped pair.

FIRINGS.

(1) rebar-autodeploy-review-interrupts [LEGACY alarm, deleted ~11:40Z] — ALARM 04:01:26Z, recovered 04:16:26Z. Driving datapoint 03:46Z bucket Sum=1. Journal marker 2026-08-12T03:59:33Z: reason=bound-exceeded, in_flight=1, deferred_for=1820s, bound=1800s, target=57d19254. TRUE POSITIVE. Boundary case: the underlying event is at 03:59:33Z, inside the greasy-plucky-piranha window that closed ~04:00Z, so this is the tail of the 4 already-triaged-and-accepted firings; only the alarm evaluation landed 86s after the baseline. Alarm behavior correct, keep as-is.

(2) rebar-autodeploy-review-interrupts [LEGACY] — ALARM 08:27:26Z, recovered 08:42:26Z. Datapoint 08:12Z bucket Sum=1. Journal marker 08:26:14Z: reason=bound-exceeded, in_flight=1, deferred_for=1810s, bound=1800s, target=1791436c. TRUE POSITIVE, genuinely new since baseline. Same class as the accepted piranha findings: the drain check WORKED, DEPLOY_DEFER_MAX was spent with a review still in flight, deploy proceeded and killed it. Alarm behavior correct, keep as-is.

(3) rebar-autodeploy-review-interrupts-bound-exceeded [NEW alarm, junco/1650] — ALARM 19:38:49Z, recovered 19:53:49Z. Datapoint 19:23Z bucket Sum=1. Journal marker 19:34:44Z: reason=bound-exceeded, in_flight=1, deferred_for=1930s, bound=1800s, target=f6f31dfd. TRUE POSITIVE, genuinely new. First real firing of the replacement alarm; it fired for the right reason with the right reason-scoped attribution. Alarm behavior correct, keep as-is.

No other alarm changed state in the window. rebar-autodeploy-review-interrupts-signal-unavailable never fired (it settled INSUFFICIENT_DATA→OK at 11:42:21Z and has stayed OK).

NEAR-MISS / NEW DEFECT (no firing, but a fabricated metric emission).
At 09:48:03Z the observability probe published in ONE run: review_interrupts_bound_exceeded=7 and review_interrupts_signal_unavailable=1. Both landed in the single minute 09:48Z (period-60 query confirms). No matching events occurred then. Evidence: journal retention reaches back to 2026-07-03T19:50:40Z, so nothing rotated away; full-journal totals are bound-exceeded=8 and signal-unavailable=1; the ONLY signal-unavailable marker in the entire journal is 2026-08-04T00:36:41Z, i.e. 5.5 days older than the run that published it as 'new this interval'.
Mechanism: infra/scripts/observability.sh publish_autodeploy_marker_delta() converts a cumulative full-journal grep -c into a per-interval delta via a persisted offset file, with prev defaulting to 0 when the file is absent. The reason-scoped counters were brand new, so their first run computed new = total = all retained history. The helper already clamps the OPPOSITE direction (negative delta / lost history, per bug 2dc7-31b7-ecbb-4cd2 and the 1648 rotation double-count clamp); the cold-start case (offset ABSENT rather than journal SHRUNK) is the complementary gap and is unguarded.
Why it did not page: the two alarms were created at 11:40:58Z, ~2h AFTER the 09:48:03Z probe run. That ordering is luck. Under the usual terraform-then-deploy order both 1-datapoint latches would have fired instantly off stale history — including the signal-unavailable alarm, whose own description calls it 'the URGENT one ... EVERY deploy is running blind', from a single already-resolved 2026-08-04 event.
Classified FALSE-POSITIVE-GENERATING metric defect, not an alarm-threshold problem: the alarm predicate is right to fire on a nonzero count, the count was fabricated. Filed as bug widespread-zealous-narwhal (e2a6-9ee4-8d5c-4290), open/unclaimed, file impact infra/scripts/observability.sh. Latent for every future counter added to the shared helper and for any offset-file loss (fresh /var/lib/rebar, host rebuild, disk restore); the same open-coded shape exists in sections 3 (replication_errors), 4 (voter_errors) and 4b (g2p_dispatch_errors).

NOISE RATE for the piranha 'accepted, retune only if pager noise becomes a problem' disposition, so it can be revisited with data rather than quietly loosened:
  Aug 1–11 (11 days): 6 review-interrupt firings — 08-04T00:09:45Z, 00:38:45Z, 01:45:45Z, 08-07T11:33:14Z, 12:55:14Z, 08-12T03:08:26Z ≈ 0.55/day.
  Aug 12 alone (00:00–22:45Z): 4 firings — 03:08:26Z, 04:01:26Z, 08:27:26Z, 19:38:49Z ≈ 10x the preceding rate, matching the 60+-merge landing burst.
All four Aug-12 journal markers cleared the bound by a hair: deferred_for 1810s / 1820s / 1810s / 1930s against bound=1800s, i.e. 10s, 20s, 10s and 130s over. Every one of them was a review that finished (or would have) shortly after the deferral budget expired. That points at DEPLOY_DEFER_MAX being marginally undersized for current review durations, NOT at the alarm being too sensitive — a bound raise is a fix to the true-positive CAUSE, not a threshold loosening, and would plausibly have prevented all four interrupts.

CORRELATION WITH KNOWN CONTEXT.
  - JIRA_API_TOKEN expiry (until ~18:30Z, healthy run 18:34Z): produced ZERO alarm firings. rebar/host:voter_errors was 0 across the entire window, and the rebar/host namespace has no reconcile/bridge counter at all (19 metric names, none bridge-related). So bridge auth failure is currently invisible to CloudWatch. Coverage gap — recommendation only, no change made.
  - Alarm replacement (junco/1650): confirmed. Both reason-scoped alarms carry AlarmConfigurationUpdatedTimestamp 2026-08-12T11:40:58Z and settled out of INSUFFICIENT_DATA at 11:41:49Z / 11:42:21Z. The legacy rolled-up alarm is gone from describe-alarms; its metric review_interrupts is still published (offset 9 = 8 bound + 1 signal), so pre-split history stays readable as designed.
  - Rotation double-count clamp (1648): not implicated in any firing; it is the sibling guard to the cold-start gap that IS implicated.
  - Heavy overnight CI/agent activity: consistent with the 10x interrupt rate; no load-metric alarm (disk, EC2 checks, bedrock, g2p, replication, mirror, merge-change) moved at all.

BOTTOM LINE: 3 firings, all TRUE POSITIVES of the same known bound-exceeded behavior — no alarm should be tuned for any of them. 1 new latent false-positive defect in metric emission, filed. 2 operator decisions surfaced: whether to raise DEPLOY_DEFER_MAX, and whether to add bridge/reconcile alarm coverage.

[2026-08-12T23:22:57Z] AWS alarm sweep ADDENDUM — follow-up firing pair triaged (read-only ops investigation)
(migrated from childsafe-bizarre-lorikeet comment 13 — session-scoped ops/analysis record; original comment retained there, see the index comment on that ticket)

ADDENDUM — follow-up firing pair triaged, 2026-08-12T23:07Z (read-only throughout).

FIRINGS (4) and (5).
  rebar-gerrit-voter-errors            ALARM 23:07:07Z -> OK 23:13:07Z, datapoint 23:06Z Sum=1
  rebar-review-bot-merge-change-errors ALARM 23:07:18Z -> OK 23:13:18Z, datapoint 23:06Z Sum=1

BOTH ARE FALSE POSITIVES. No voter error and no merge-change error occurred. Both counts trace to a
SINGLE journal line at 2026-08-12T23:02:26Z (CONTAINER_NAME=compose-review-bot-1) which is the
review-bot's own LLM code-review analysis prose, verbatim:

    ...mits matching markers for every target (VOTER_ERROR, MERGE_CHANGE_ERROR, AUTODEPLOY_ERROR,
    AUTODEPLOY_DEFERRED, gerrit_to_platform error, both interrupt reasons) and REPL_LOG is
    populated. The rolled-up review_interrupts per_interval=2 arithmetic is consistent
    (total 14 seeded, next run +2)

Nothing redacted; the line contains no secret. The reviewer was reviewing a change to
infra/scripts/observability.sh ITSELF — the cold-start seeding fix for widespread-zealous-narwhal
filed earlier in this same sweep — so it enumerated the marker vocabulary as prose, and the probe
counted that prose as two errors.

MECHANISM. observability.sh sections 4 and 4c count markers with an UNANCHORED grep over the
review-bot container journal (grep -cE 'VOTER_ERROR' / 'MERGE_CHANGE_ERROR'). The review-bot writes
its LLM output to that same stream, so the probe cannot distinguish its own alarm vocabulary from an
actual error.

PROOF IT IS NOT A REAL MARKER (full-journal counts; real markers are line-start under -o cat):
  VOTER_ERROR        line-start real: 221   substring-anywhere: 222   offset file: 222
  MERGE_CHANGE_ERROR line-start real:   0   substring-anywhere:   1   offset file:   1
Exactly one of the 222 voter counts is the false match. The merge-change counter has NEVER recorded
a real error in the entire retained journal — its ONLY count in history is this false positive, and
that is what fired its alarm.

COORDINATOR HYPOTHESIS REFUTED. The proposed cause (a patchset superseding a mid-review change 409ing
the bot's vote or merge call, amid the 1684-1688 push/review activity) does not hold: there is no
409, no conflict and no Gerrit 4xx/5xx of any kind in 22:45-23:20Z. The trigger was textual, not a
Gerrit interaction.

RECOVERY / STATE. Nothing was left in a bad state and nothing needed retrying, because nothing
failed. The review-bot voted normally before, during and after the alarm window — voter_voted at
23:05:08Z, 23:13:04Z, 23:19:38Z. The counters 'self-cleared' only because the offset absorbed the
one-time count; that is arithmetic, not recovery. Side effect: the offset files are now permanently
inflated by the false count (voter offset 222 vs 221 real markers).

CLASSIFICATION: NEW DEFECT, and the alarms are NOT at fault — both are correct to fire on a nonzero
count; the count was fabricated. Do not tune either alarm. Filed as colossal-slothful-grouse
(8c2f-8377-5044-4650), open/unclaimed, file impact infra/scripts/observability.sh.

RELATION TO widespread-zealous-narwhal: same false-positive FAMILY (probe publishes counts for
non-events) but a DISTINCT mechanism — narwhal is an absent-offset cold start, grouse is an
over-broad pattern matching the token as data. Both in observability.sh.

RECURRENCE RISK IS ACTIVE AND SELF-REFERENTIAL. The trigger is any review that discusses
observability.sh or the marker vocabulary, and the fleet is landing observability.sh changes right
now (the narwhal fix is in review — its review text is literally what fired this). Expect these two
alarms to re-fire on each further review of that file until grouse is fixed.

RUNNING TALLY for this sweep: 5 firings since the 04:00Z baseline — 3 true-positive bound-exceeded
review interrupts (no tuning warranted) and 2 false positives from probe-side defects; 2 new bugs
filed (widespread-zealous-narwhal, colossal-slothful-grouse), both in infra/scripts/observability.sh.
